nom: EltaMD UV AOX Elements Tinted Mineral Face Sunscreen Lotion

segments.dry: The one reviewer who names dry skin found the sunscreen left her face extremely tight and highlighted dry, scabbing patches, and guessed it might suit oily skin better than hers.
segments.oily: Oily-skin reviewers are split: several say it controls shine and doesn't break them out over hours of wear, while one describes it as too heavy for oily skin specifically in hot summer weather.
segments.sensitive: Reviewers with sensitive, rosacea-prone, or eczema-affected skin generally report good tolerance of the mineral formula with no burning, but the most severe reactions in the reviews — a face-and-neck rash requiring steroids, and immediate irritation traced to an inactive ingredient — also come from this group, both tied to the recent reformulation.
segments.combination: The one reviewer describing combination, slightly dehydrated skin reports a beautiful finish with no issues.
segments.mature: Reviewers describing mature skin use it as a 2-in-1 moisturizer and foundation replacement, crediting it with deep hydration and help managing stubborn pigmentation.

concerns.aging: The only concrete comment on aging is cosmetic rather than treatment-related: one reviewer notes it doesn't settle into wrinkles or fine lines throughout the day, unlike some foundations.
concerns.dehydration: Most reviewers describe the finish as hydrating or dewy rather than drying, including one with dehydrated combination skin; the exception is a dry-skin reviewer who found it left her face feeling tight and emphasized dry patches for at least an hour after application.
concerns.redness: Several reviewers report it evens out redness cosmetically or doesn't burn medicated or rosacea-prone skin, but the two most negative reviews in the set — a severe facial and neck rash requiring prescription steroids, and immediate irritation from an inactive ingredient — both describe serious redness reactions tied to the reformulated version.
concerns.barrier: One reviewer with eczema, whose skin reacts to chemical sunscreen filters, tolerates this mineral formula well, though a separate review notes the reformulated version now includes an added chemical UV filter, which could matter for reactive skin going forward.
concerns.spots: Reviewers managing melasma or hyperpigmentation use this as their daily sunscreen and report the tint camouflages dark spots and pigmentation, though this reads as coverage rather than a fading or treatment effect.
concerns.blemishes: Reviewers with acne-prone skin report no new breakouts, though one reviewer notes explicitly that the tint is too sheer to actually cover blemishes, only to even out redness.
concerns.oiliness: Oily-skin reviewers mostly report it keeps shine controlled through the day without feeling greasy, though one reviewer found it too heavy and oily-feeling specifically in hot, humid summer conditions.

aspects.libelle: Pump dispenser frequently jams or fails midway through the bottle
Recent reformulation shifted the tint noticeably more orange
Bottle size shrank while the price increased
Light, non-greasy texture that blends like a tinted foundation
New formula added a chemical UV filter alongside the minerals
Water-resistant and long-wearing through sweat or exercise

extraits.titre: Terrible breakout!! Read the bad reviews!!!!
extraits.texte: So I LOVED this sunscreen until my recent reorder. I thought I was getting the same product when I hit reorder but when it showed up the SPF was higher and the packaging was different. Figured I was getting an even better version of what I loved with an updated look. Boy was I wrong. Whatever changed in the formula sent my skin into an absolute tailspin. I’m on day 4 of a rash that covers my entire face, neck, chest, ears, and back of my neck that top of my shoulders. It is clear where the sunscreen was because that’s where I have puss filled whelps, and the rash spread beyond that area but isn’t as severe where I didn’t have the sunscreen. I’m having to take prescription steroids for the first time in my life & put on antibiotic gel twice a day. I live in Texas and I work outdoors. My livelihood is dependent on working in the sun and currently I can’t let the sun touch my skin, and if I get warm or close to sweating my skin gets worse. I literally look like a swamp creature and am beyond uncomfortable. I rarely leave reviews but whoever’s idea it was to exchange these products as equals should know they really messed up my skin. Beware of what you order and if you get a “new version” or different packaging make sure you check the ingredient percentages before using it. I guess I shouldn’t be so trusting. Truly disappointed. Wish I had read the bad reviews before reordering. SO MANY PEOPLE have had this problem! Ugh!

My dermatologist recommended this sunscreen to add into my skin care routine of tretinoin and clindamycin phosphate, I washed my face ,added the climdamycin, a thin layer of my moisturizer because I have dry skin, and then lastly added this sunscreen. I was so excited to try it because I thought it was gonna work out great, but immediately after applying my face felt so extremely tight. I looked in the mirror and it’s making any acne marks that are healing look super dry, it’s highlighting some scabbing I have and it doesn’t look glowy at all on my skin. It’s been an hour since application and my skin still feels tight. Maybe this would work out Great for someone with oily skin but it didn’t work out for me😢😢😢SO SAD! Back to my sunscreen quest. Also paid 40$ which is a lot just for it to not work. About to get that refund yall. TINT isn’t bad though as you can see in the pictures it doesn’t look orange or anything and I have rather fair complexion. ALSO IT SMELLS SO BAD! Put it on and every time I went outside I got this terrible wiff of dank sunscreen. Smelt so bad wanted to take it off immediately. Sunscreen smell was so bad throughout the day.

extraits.titre: Easy to blend and good for sensitive skin
extraits.texte: This is my favorite tinted mineral sunscreen so far. I've tried the Colorscience (Flex, Medium) before, but that one is too dark for my complexion. This one's just right. My problem with this is that it gets cakey when I reapply. So, I am hoping to find a new one. Unfortunately, since I have eczema, my skin reacts to chemical sunscreen. I've already tried the Japanese and Korean ones. I love their formula, my skin does not. Another thing I don't like about the product is the price just keeps going up! It's crazy!

Filipina girl here with brown skin. Skin type: oily I LOVE this sunscreen! It has a medium-thick consistency. It blends perfectly into my skin, dries down quick, and doesn’t leave me greasy. A few hours later, I’m not looking oily. It somehow also helps keep my oils under control. Definitely going to repurchase!

This is my everyday sunscreen! I’m prone to melasma and dark spots, so my dermatologist recommended wearing sunscreen every day, preferably SPF 50 or higher. I love that this one is tinted, which gives me light coverage and works almost like a foundation, so I don’t need to apply an additional foundation when I’m in a hurry. It’s also not too oily, and I simply finish with a little loose powder to set it. It feels comfortable, provides the coverage I want, and is easy to incorporate into my daily routine. Highly recommended!

An excellent 2-in-1 moisturizer and sunscreen for mature skin. It simplifies my morning routine by replacing a light foundation, protecting against stubborn pigmentation, and delivering the deep hydration my skin needs. Keeps me protected from the sunny beach all day.
